title: Absorb the restricted monomial by the four-bit gate (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

#4517 already answered the operator-norm question in #4515. Its open step is the scalar comparison. Replacing the base `9 p^2 + ε` in #4506 by `9 p^2` gives

```text
2 g (9 p^2)^{g-1} p^6 exp(K p - p^2) < 2^{-C p}
```

for integers `p ≥ 2`, `g ≥ 1`, `K ≥ 0` and `C ≥ 0`, whenever `p ≥ max(64, 4K + 2C)` and `16 g ceil(log2 p) ≤ p`.

The factor 2 is one bit added to the #4496 exponent. Eight times the new exponent is at most `-16`, so the exponent is at most `-C p - 2`. Four bits still majorize 9 because `9 < 16`. Three bits still fail because `9 > 8`. At `g = p^2` the monomial is greater than 1.

This absorbs the scalar only. It does not prove `||C_i|| ≤ 9 p^2` or `||P_glob - C_i||_2 < p^6 exp(-p^2)`. Both ideal-gap gauges stay hypotheses. No new κ. The selected record remains `23/10000`.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-restricted-gate`
- [x] Prints `PASS_GAUSSIAN_RESTRICTED_GATE` and `outcome=completed`
- [ ] Maintainer replay was not run

Base `f9f85c1e4fa1e955ff39f10fca447e3e2a4e4adc`, priority revision 7. Upstream fetched at 2026-10-22T03:18:46Z was that commit, and the pre-submit fetch at 2026-10-22T03:22:35Z was unchanged. κ remains `23/10000`.
